## R Markdown

In class work for Week-4

```{r}
n_values <- c(1, 5, 20, 100)
B <- 10000

colors <- c("blue", "green", "orange", "purple")

# Set up an empty plot
plot(
  NA,
  xlim = c(-4, 4),
  ylim = c(0, 1),
  xlab = "x",
  ylab = "CDF",
  main = "Convergence in Distribution to N(0,1)"
)

for (i in 1:length(n_values)) {

  n <- n_values[i]

  x <- rnorm(
    B,
    mean = 0,
    sd = sqrt(1 + 1/n)
  )

  F_hat <- ecdf(x)

  curve(
    F_hat(x),
    from = -4,
    to = 4,
    add = TRUE,
    col = colors[i],
    lwd = 2
  )
}

# Limiting theoretical CDF
curve(
  pnorm(x),
  from = -4,
  to = 4,
  add = TRUE,
  col = "black",
  lwd = 3,
  lty = 2
)

legend(
  "topleft",
  legend = c(
    paste("n =", n_values),
    "N(0,1)"
  ),
  col = c(colors, "black"),
  lwd = c(rep(2, 4), 3),
  lty = c(rep(1, 4), 2),
  bty = "n"
)


mtext(
  "Convergence in Distribution to N(0,1)",
  outer = TRUE,
  cex = 1.3
)

```



```{r}

sample_size = c(10,50,100,1000)
n = 100
sim_size = 10000

par(
  mfrow = c(2, 2),
  oma = c(0, 0, 3, 0),
  mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1), 
  las = 1
)

for (i in 1:length(sample_size)){
  n <- sample_size[i]
  xbar <- numeric(n)  # pre-allocate x_bar, since it's being updated element by element.
                       
for (j in 1:sim_size){

  x <- rnorm(n,5,2)
  xbar[j] <- mean(x)


}

  hist(xbar,
       probability = TRUE,
       breaks = 50,
       xlim = c(2,9),
       main = paste("n = ",n)
       )
  
}

```
```{r}

# Same as above execpt using the replicate function 

sample_size <- c(10, 50, 100, 1000)
sim_size <- 10000

par(
  mfrow = c(2, 2),
  oma = c(0, 0, 3, 0),
  mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1),
  las = 1
)

for (i in 1:length(sample_size)) {

  n <- sample_size[i]

  xbar <- replicate(       # Note, replicate is creating the vector
    sim_size,              # then filling it.  
    mean(rnorm(n, 5, 2))
  )

  hist(
    xbar,
    probability = TRUE,
    breaks = 50,
    xlim = c(2, 9),
    main = paste("n =", n)
  )
}

```

```{r}
set.seed(123)

x <- rnorm(1000)
n <- length(x)

# Empirical quantile function
plot(
    (1:n) / n,  # plots along the x-axis - normalizes n to 1
    sort(x),    # plots along the y-axis - returns the order statistic of x=rnorm
    type = "s", # draw as a step function 
    xlab = "p",
    ylab = "Quantile",
    main = "Empirical vs. Theoretical Normal Quantile Function"
)

# Theoretical standard normal quantile function
p <- seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 1000)

lines(
    p,
    qnorm(p),    # apply inverse-phi to the list of quantiles, takes a prob and returns a point on the z-axis 
    col = "red",
    lwd = 2
)

```
